title: Archive and Colony
premise: Yara Lockridge smuggles forbidden memories between the warring fleets of Meridian and Halcyon, worlds severed by a war neither side remembers starting. When a deep-space vessel returns with its crew aged backward and carrying a memory that proves the war was manufactured, Yara is blackmailed by both governments into retrieving it. Falling in love with the ship's de-aged navigator, Sef, she must choose between delivering the truth that could reignite open war or preserving a lie that keeps an uneasy peace. In the end she broadcasts the true memory during a fleet standoff, sacrificing her smuggling network and nearly her life, but forcing both worlds to confront their shared guilt — and choosing Sef and her ragtag crew over any flag.
about_author: Wren Villalobos is a former radio archivist who writes science fiction about what societies choose to forget. They live aboard a converted cargo barge and claim their best plot ideas arrive during engine maintenance.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She runs contraband memories through the quarantine gap between Meridian and Halcyon, establishing her crew: gruff engineer Doss, teenage hacker Pip, and the AI ghost of her dead mentor. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness; she memorizes other people's pasts because she refuses to keep her own.

chapters.title: Customs at the Broken Gate
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A near-miss inspection forces her to swallow a client's memory chip raw, showing readers how memory-smuggling works and what it costs her body. She glimpses a military convoy escorting something toward derelict Station Vesper. Emotional beat: fear sharpened into defiance.

chapters.title: What Came Back
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The deep-space survey ship Anemone returns after forty years away — but its crew are children in adult bodies, aged backward by whatever they found. Sef, now physically nineteen again, watches his captain interrogated like a criminal. Emotional beat: disorientation and grief for a life already lived.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Both governments summon her separately: each believes the other has weaponized the Anemone's secret. Each offers to erase her criminal record; each threatens her crew. Emotional beat: the trap closing, loyalty to her found family tested against self-preservation.

chapters.title: The De-Aged Man
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Detained on Station Vesper, Sef meets Yara when she's smuggled in to extract his testimony. He recognizes her as the courier who once carried his sister's last message. Emotional beat: wary connection between two people who trade in other people's truths.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The extraction goes wrong — Sef's backward-aged mind stores memories in fragments, and pulling one triggers a seizure that floods Yara with his forty years of deep space. She sees the thing they found: a beacon broadcasting the war's true origin. Emotional beat: intimacy forced open too fast.

chapters.title: Doss's Bargain
chapters.summary: Doss's POV. While Yara recovers from memory-flood, Doss negotiates with a Meridian admiral to protect Pip, unknowingly selling information about Yara's route. Emotional beat: love curdling into betrayal; Doss believes he's saving the family, not dooming it.

chapters.title: Forty Years in One Night
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Recovering, Sef tells Yara the full story of the Anemone's voyage — the beacon's recording proving both fleets were manipulated into war by a third party long dissolved. Emotional beat: quiet falling-in-love over shared witness; two people who carry what others cannot hold.

chapters.title: Pip's Discovery
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. The youngest crew member cracks the beacon's encryption and finds a second layer: the countdown isn't on the station reactor — it's on the beacon itself, which will purge its own record in nine days. Emotional beat: youthful triumph shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: The Lie That Holds
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara realizes the official story — that the Anemone returned empty and cursed — is the only thing keeping the fleets from fighting over its secret. Telling the truth might start the war it should end. Emotional beat: the weight of custody; duty versus truth made literal.

chapters.title: Halcyon's Offer
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Halcyon intelligence offers Sef restoration of his true age in exchange for the beacon coordinates — and for naming Yara as his source. Emotional beat: temptation of wholeness against loyalty to someone he's known nine days but shared forty years of memory with.

chapters.title: Vesper Burns
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Meridian raids Station Vesper to seize the Anemone; the crew escapes in the chaos but Doss is captured covering their retreat. Emotional beat: the cost of the lie becomes blood; Yara learns Doss bargained with the enemy and can't decide if it was treason or sacrifice.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Hiding in a smuggler drift, Yara consults her mentor's AI ghost, who reveals he helped manufacture the original cover-up decades ago. Emotional beat: found family's foundations cracked; even her chosen inheritance is built on the lie.

chapters.title: The Reactor Countdown
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Pip discovers Station Vesper's failing reactor will detonate when the beacon purges — the two systems were linked deliberately, a dead-man's switch. Seven days. Emotional beat: adolescent terror transmuted into resolve; Pip stops being the kid of the crew.

chapters.title: Interrogation of Doss
chapters.summary: Doss's POV. Under Meridian interrogation, Doss gives up nothing about Yara but confirms the beacon exists, escalating both fleets' mobilization. He understands he's started the war he tried to prevent. Emotional beat: guilt as a form of love; protecting family by becoming the villain.

chapters.title: Nine Days of Peace
chapters.summary: Sef and Yara's alternating POV. A stolen interlude in the drift while Pip reroutes the beacon: Sef teaches Yara the deep-space songs his older self loved; Yara shows Sef the memories worth keeping. Emotional beat: love fully admitted, knowing it may be brief.

chapters.title: Both Flags at the Gate
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The Meridian and Halcyon fleets converge on the Broken Gate, each believing the other will fire first. Yara's old clients beg her to run. Emotional beat: the loneliest moment — every door closed except the one leading into the crossfire.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax, Yara's POV. Yara flies her smuggler straight between the fleets and transmits the beacon's full record — the manufactured war, the manipulation, both governments' complicity — on every open channel, as the reactor countdown hits zero and Vesper detonates behind her like a signature. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into certainty; the lie dies so the peace can be born honest.

chapters.title: Aftermath at the Gate
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The fleets stand down in stunned silence; admirals on both sides scramble to control the narrative, but the crews have heard everything. Doss is released in the confusion. Emotional beat: exhausted, fragile hope; the war didn't end, it just stopped being inevitable.

chapters.title: What the Truth Costs
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Tribunals loom; Yara surrenders her smuggling network and accepts trial rather than let her crew take the fall. Sef refuses age-restoration treatment, choosing the man he is now. Emotional beat: grief and release; paying debts without regret.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. At the joint hearing, testimony from the Anemone's de-aged crew — children with veterans' eyes — turns public opinion. Yara is convicted of smuggling but pardoned for the broadcast; Doss takes a work detail beside her. Emotional beat: justice imperfect but real; accountability as the first act of the new peace.

chapters.title: Archive and Colony
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Yara's POV. A year later, Yara, Sef, Doss, and Pip run a legitimate courier line between Meridian and Halcyon, carrying open archives instead of contraband. The beacon's site becomes a memorial colony where both worlds' children study the war together. Emotional beat: homecoming not to a place but to people; love chosen over duty, and duty remade by love.
